record.paper_title: SYMMETRY AND COLORINGS: SOME RESULTS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
record.original_question: For the integer lattice Zⁿ with n > 3, calculate the numbers χ(Zⁿ) that govern the exact minimal-central-set calculations in this setting, and determine the structure of central sets in Zⁿ.

evidence.quote: In this section given a group G we consider two questions: (1) what is the structure of central subsets of G and (2) what is the minimal size c(G) of a central set in G?
2.4. Problem ( [2]). Calculate the numbers χ(Zn) and investigate the structure of central sets in Zn for n > 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a group. For an element g ∈ G, define the involution s_g : G → G by s_g(x) = gx^{-1}g. A subset C ⊆ G is called symmetric with center g if s_g(C) = C, equivalently if gC^{-1}g = C. A finite subset C ⊆ G with |C| ≥ 2 is called central if for every finite subset F ⊆ G there exists h ∈ G such that hF h ⊆ ⋃_{c ∈ C} c·G·c (more precisely, a central set is one that meets every symmetric subset of G of sufficiently large size; equivalently, C is central if every finite coloring of G in which C is monochromatic admits a monochromatic symmetric subset of arbitrarily large size). Define
   χ(G) = min{ |C| : C ⊆ G is a central subset of G }.
For the abelian group G = Z^n with n > 3, determine the value of χ(Z^n) and describe the structure (up to translation and the natural action of GL_n(Z)) of all central subsets of Z^n.
artifact.status_search_result: No published computation of χ(Z^n) for n > 3 or classification of central sets in Z^n for n > 3 was found. Related work by Banakh, Protasov, Verbitsky and Vorobets addresses symmetric monochromatic subsets and coloring numbers of abelian groups, but the specific values χ(Z^n) for n > 3 and a structural description of central sets in higher-dimensional integer lattices appear to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Banakh, Verbitsky, Vorobets study symmetric monochromatic subsets and coloring invariants of abelian groups including Z^n.
status_evidence.claim: The framework for central/symmetric sets in Z^n is developed but exact values of χ(Z^n) for n > 3 are not given.

status_evidence.title: The covering number of the difference sets in partitions of G-spaces and groups
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of partial results on Protasov's problems concerning partitions of groups; no full resolution for Z^n, n>3.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to treat related Protasov problems as open.
